title: Quarterly roadmap playlist: sprint-map for Hosted API & Model Catalog
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a compact, executable quarterly "playlist" (sprint-map) that sequences Hosted API feature work and Model Catalog onboards across three release tranches. The playlist should: 1) prioritize model variants and gating criteria for each tranche; 2) define canary windows, metrics and rollback thresholds; 3) map infra dependencies (autoscale, routing fallbacks, KV cache configs) into sprint owners; and 4) include buffer lanes for overflow capacity. This ticket synthesizes inputs from research (latency/cost trade studies), Eng runtime constraints, and sales-identified cohorts to produce a deliverable weekly sprint map and a stakeholder-ready Q2 launch sequence.
acceptance_criteria: Sprint-map document with week-by-week commitments across 8 weeks is published to Confluence
Model Catalog tranche list with gating criteria (eval pass rate, perf delta, token cost delta) for each model is agreed by Research and Eng
Canary policy template (metrics, alert thresholds, automatic fallback decision tree) is reviewed and signed off by SRE
All ENG dependencies have owners and rough estimates in the sprint map
Risk buffer lanes and contingency triggers are documented and mapped to on-call playbooks
progress_updates: 2026-03-01: Kickoff meeting with Product, Eng infra, Research and Solutions. Aligned on three tranche approach and primary success metrics (p95 latency, unit token cost, eval quality delta).

2026-03-02: Drafted tranche criteria. Research proposed initial eval thresholds: >= 95% baseline answer agreement on core prompt set; perf delta < +15% token cost for common seq lengths. Note: engineering flagged that L1 quantized variants need runtime validation for KV cache behavior.
2026-03-03: Eng leads (runtime/scheduling) estimated work for tranche A canary pipeline: 3 dev-weeks + 1 week of integration tests. Added dependency ENG-3920 for canary automation hooks.
2026-03-04: SRE reviewed canary metrics list; requested inclusion of request-rate abrasion tests and a latency-stress threshold. Added alert runbook stub.
2026-03-05: Updated sprint-map with week-level owners and added a contingency buffer (two days per tranche) to accommodate unexpected kernel tuning regressions.
review_feedback: PM feedback (Evelyn Morales): tighten tranche naming to avoid ambiguity between 'canary' and 'pilot'; prefer 'Tranche A - Pilot', 'Tranche B - Ramp', 'Tranche C - Scale'.
Design feedback (Samir Rao): need a customer-facing migration note for existing hosted endpoints when model overload fallback occurs.
Engineering feedback (Ritu Shah): recommend a small pre-canary 'staging soak' on dedicated infra to catch KV cache cold-start regressions before opening canary to customers.
SRE feedback (Darnell Hayes): define explicit rollback criteria and automated switch-to-fallback policy; currently the document has manual steps only.
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Decision: Use three tranches to balance risk and velocity; Pilot will target low-traffic cohorts only to minimize blast radius.
Tradeoff: Accept a slightly longer runway (add two buffer days per tranche) to enable kernel-level regressions to be resolved, which increases time-to-scale but reduces outage risk.
Decision: Prioritize model variants that show <=10% token-cost regression and pass per-prompt evals; defer experimental quantized variants to Tranche B to avoid canary complexity.
next_steps: Finalize week-by-week sprint-map and publish Confluence doc by 2026-03-07
ENG: Create ENG-3920 (canary automation) and ENG-3987 (staging-soak pipeline) with owners assigned
Research: Freeze the core eval prompt set and publish gating thresholds by 2026-03-09
SRE: Draft automated rollback playbook and wire alerts into PagerDuty by 2026-03-14
PM: Prepare partner-facing release notes and migration guidance for hosted API customers prior to Tranche B launch
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Kernel-level regressions when introducing quantized variants could increase latency spikes. Mitigation: staging soak and extended buffer + kernel-level smoke tests.
Risk: Insufficient capacity during scale-up window. Mitigation: reserve Dedicated burst pool as contingency and include capacity toggle in console rollout UI.
Risk: Eval regressions discovered post-canary. Mitigation: block Tranche B unless eval pass rate maintained for 72-hour rolling window on canary cohort.
notes_for_engineering: Ensure canary pipeline exposes token-level cost and p95 latency per model variant; include KV cache hit-rate as a primary signal.
Add a feature-flagged capacity toggle for Dedicated burst pool and document fallthrough routing behavior.
Provide an automated smoke test that verifies prefix caching and KV cache integrity on quantized builds before canary starts.
